📋 Platform Rules: Dos & Don'ts · Lesson 5 of 7

X (Twitter): The Dos, Don'ts & Suspension Mistakes

6 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

Since 8 September 2026, X only pays for original posts. Put 'Wueh, look at this 😂' on someone else's viral video and it earns you nothing, however many views it gets.

X replaced Creator Revenue Sharing with the Original Content Rewards programme. To qualify you must be 18 or older, pay for Premium, Premium+ or Premium Business, have at least 500 verified followers, and get 500,000 home-timeline views from verified users in 90 days. Only Premium users' impressions count, and you have to keep meeting the bar to keep getting paid. Check in the app whether it's open in your country before you pay for Premium.

Kenya has history here. A 2021 Mozilla Foundation study found about 3,700 accounts behind at least 11 paid 'hashtag for hire' campaigns, with some influencers paid around $10–15 a day via M-Pesa. Twitter then took action against more than 100 Kenyan accounts under its platform manipulation policy.

DODON'T
Post your own writing, photos, reporting and memesRepost viral clips with a caption that just describes them
Use one or two hashtags that fit the postHijack a trending national hashtag to sell your wigs or phones
Reply thoughtfully to people you followSend bulk, unsolicited replies, mentions or DMs
Run separate accounts for separate purposes (X allows up to ten that don't duplicate each other)Use several accounts to boost the same posts or push a trend
Follow people whose posts you actually readFollow and unfollow in bulk to pad your numbers
Argue hard about ideasTarget people with abuse, or communities with ethnic insults
Mark parody and fan accounts clearlyPose as a real person, company or government office
Keep your handle and account yoursBuy or sell accounts or handles. That can mean instant suspension
Verify before you post breaking newsShare fake documents or doctored clips, especially in protest or election periods
Disclose paid posts clearlyTake money to push a political hashtag without saying so

What X's rules say gets you restricted

X's platform manipulation and spam policy bans inflating likes, reposts or poll votes (including through third-party apps), buying or selling followers or engagement, follow churn, coordinated activity across fake or automated accounts, and hashtag or keyword spam.

The honest risk ladder for bought engagement

  1. Reduced visibility. Posts are hidden from parts of X or kept out of recommendations.
  2. Anti-spam challenges. The account is locked until you verify a phone number or solve a reCAPTCHA.
  3. Feature limits and forced deletions. Posting, DMs, Spaces or Live can be restricted, or you're told to delete posts before you can carry on.
  4. Permanent suspension. For repeat offences, or straight away for severe ones such as selling accounts.
💡 The detail most people miss

Buying followers is named in X's policy, and so is selling them. A creator who resells engagement or 'trend slots' to others is breaking the same rule on the other side. And the payout bar counts verified followers and Premium users' views, which cheap bulk followers usually aren't.

Kenyan specifics

  • Elections 2027. The NCIC says online posts carry the same legal consequences as public speeches, and it has called on influencers to show restraint.
  • Cyber law. The High Court's July 2026 ruling removed the 'likely to cause suicide' clause and NC4's power to block websites without a court. Harassment, phishing and identity-theft offences under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act still apply.
  • Paid trends. Pushing a hashtag for cash without disclosure breaks X's rules on coordinated activity. If a campaign spreads ethnic hatred, it can also break the NCIC Act.
✗ MYTH

Using hashtags gets you shadowbanned on X.

✓ REALITY

X's policy targets excessive, unrelated hashtags and hijacking trends to push something. One or two relevant tags are fine. The thing that actually reduces visibility is spammy behaviour: bulk replies, duplicate posts, and coordinated accounts.

✅ Your 10-minute rules audit
⚡ Quick check

Under X's Original Content Rewards, which of these earns you nothing?

X counts your own writing, photos, reporting and memes, plus clips you add real commentary to or creatively edit. A caption that just describes someone else's video doesn't qualify.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. X now pays only for original content, and only from verified users' impressions.
  2. Buying, selling, follow churn, trend hijacking and multi-account boosting are all named violations.
  3. The ladder runs reduced visibility, then challenges, then feature limits, then suspension.
  4. In Kenya, election-season posts and paid political trends carry legal risk as well as platform risk.
